messages:
Sam: FYI I'm kicking off the rollforward for the panel-tiling decomposition in staging at 15:00 UTC. Main goals: validate RBAC gating, observe query batching behavior, and sanity-check latency regression windows. I'll do a 10% canary then ramp.

Jordan: Which services are in-scope for the rollout? router / projector / projection-store? Any schema changes?

Sam: router + panel-projector + authz-cache. No schema changes to primary projection tables. We'll add a small metadata table `panel_tiling_v2` to track tile ownership (read-only for now). Canary deploy uses feature-flag `panel_tiling_v2=true` so production traffic remains unchanged until we flip.

Mira: Concern: authz-cache invalidation. If we switch tiling, we might serve stale perms for a few seconds and end up returning empty panels. Recommend versioned cache keys (eg `authz:{user_id}:v3`) and a short TTL during cutover. Also add a fast path that bypasses cache for 403->200 double-checks for the canary users.

Kevin: Agreed on versioning. I'd rather not bypass cache too often — we should instead implement a conditional revalidation: on cache-miss or cache-403, async revalidate and return soft-fail with partial data + `X-Partial-Panel: true` header. That keeps p99 latency bounded.

Jordan: How are we measuring query batching changes? My worry: tiling will increase small fanout queries and break current batching heuristics.

Sam: We'll enable telemetry flags in staging: `tiling.fanout.trace=true` which surfaces per-request batch size and wait windows. Plan: compare baseline against tiling canary for 1 hour, check average batch size, p95/p99 token latencies, and cost per 1000 panels. I've wired a dashboard panel (staging -> Playback > PanelTiling Rollforward) with alerts for >10% p99 regression.

Mira: Migration and ownership: if we create `panel_tiling_v2`, we need a backfill job. Kevin, can your team run a low-priority backfill that writes `owner_hint` for existing panels? We'll mark it low IO and rate-limit.

Kevin: Yes. I'll schedule the backfill job as a batch job with concurrency=4 and an opt-in flag. We'll also emit a metric `panel_tiling.backfill.progress`.

Sam: CI/deploy plan: 1) deploy projector with feature flag off; 2) run backfill; 3) enable canary 10% for 30m; 4) validate RBAC + batching metrics; 5) ramp 50% then 100%. Rollback trie: flip flag off -> projector continues to serve old code path.

deploy-bot: Sam triggered rollout job `rollforward/panel-tiling/2209876543` (canary=10%). See https://ci.redwood/rollforward/2209876543

ci-bot: Canary deployment succeeded on region us-west-2 (10% traffic). Tests: smoke passed, load sanity ok.

Mira: During canary, let's add a short-lived synthetic traffic profile that hits RBAC edge-cases (expired tokens, org-role swaps). I can produce a set of synthetic users for that.

Sam: Good idea. @Mira please push the synthetic set to staging and tag the dashboard. Also add a quick audit log query to check for unexpected 403 spikes: `select count(*) from audit.logs where action='panel.query' and status=403 and ts > now()-interval '5 minutes'`.

Jordan: One last thing — interface boundary: projector->router contract needs an explicit `tile_version` header so routers can route to compatible caches. Let's add `X-Tile-Version: v2` and make it required for any request from projector when feature flag on. Backward compatible: default to `v1` if missing.

Sam: OK we'll add that header and document it in the API spec. Action items: Sam deploy, Kevin backfill, Mira synthetic tests + authz checks, Jordan verify batching dashboard queries. We'll reconvene after 30m canary.

Kevin: I'll own rollback playbook in case TTL misconfiguration causes denial.

Sam: Thanks team. Will post updates here during the rollforward. :rocket:
